title: High-Density Penetrating Microelectrode Recordings from Anesthetized Feline Dorsal Root Ganglia
author: Zachariah J Sperry
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.w5nfg5e
materials: Pattern tapered trenches onto silicon wafer.

Analyze raw neural data using IronClust software. Details of using this software are available at the repository. IronClust requires MATLABb 2016 or later. IronClust 4.3.3 Microsoft Windows 10 GitHub James Jun MATLAB 2017a Microsoft Windows 10 Company Website Mathworks As of 6/21/2020, IronClust is still being supported and updated for new versions of MATLAB. Use the latest available versions of both software packages and contact the developer with issues using the Github repository.
Lift-off pattern gold/platiunum interconnect lines (2.5 µm wide).

Use the micromanipulator and linear actuator software controller (included with actuator) to lower the shuttle tip about 5 mm above the surface of the target DRG, using the USB microscope for visualization
Use the linear actuator software to slowly retract the shuttle, watching to ensure array is not moving with shuttle. Jiggle back and forth as needed.

steps.title: Bond array to circuit board
steps.instruction: Bond the array interconnects to the circuit board and connect to the Omnetics Nano Dual Row Horizontal Surface Mount Tail (36‑pin, part NPD‑36‑AA).

steps.title: Move subject to support stand
steps.instruction: Place the animal on a custom 80/20‑built support stand with an overhead rack that can lower the legs below the thorax.

steps.title: Anesthetize animal and maintain physiology
steps.instruction: Inject ketamine 6.6 mg kg⁻¹, butorphanol 0.66 mg kg⁻¹, and dexmedetomidine 0.033 mg kg⁻¹ intramuscularly; intubate and maintain isoflurane at 3 % (range 2‑4 %) volume. Insert IV line(s) in one or both cephalic veins and infuse a 1:1 mixture of lactated Ringer’s solution and 5 % dextrose at 5–10 ml kg⁻¹ h⁻¹, increasing up to 30 ml kg⁻¹ h⁻¹ as needed. Continuously monitor respiratory rate, heart rate, end‑tidal CO₂, and O₂ perfusion with a Surgivet Advisor monitor and adjust anesthesia and temperature to keep the animal in a deep plane per IACUC protocol.

steps.title: Mount recording apparatus to motor adaptor
steps.instruction: Attach the shuttle jig, circuit‑board holder, circuit board, and array to the motor adaptor and secure with a 6‑32 set screw (3/8" 6‑3218‑8 stainless‑steel cup‑point).

steps.title: Activate sensory neurons (optional)
steps.instruction: Activate sensory neurons by bladder cystometry, dermatome brushing, or pudendal/pelvic nerve cuff stimulation; use the Ripple system and Trellis software for neural recording.

steps.title: Spin lower polyimide layer
steps.instruction: Spin a 2.2 µm thick lower layer of polyimide (HD Microsystems PI‑2610) onto a 4" silicon wafer.

steps.title: Spin upper polyimide layer
steps.instruction: Spin a second 2.2 µm thick layer of polyimide (PI‑2610) onto the same wafer.

steps.title: Apply titanium dioxide adhesion layer
steps.instruction: Deposit a thin titanium‑dioxide adhesion layer (applied twice) over the polyimide stack.

steps.title: Pattern array structure and contacts
steps.instruction: Pattern the outer array structure and contact openings using a hard mask followed by O₂ plasma etching.

steps.title: Deposit Ti‑Pt‑Ir contact stack
steps.instruction: Use liftoff patterning to deposit the titanium‑platinum‑iridium contact site stack.

steps.title: Fill trenches with UNCD via CVD
steps.instruction: Fill the patterned trenches with moderately conformal ultrananocrystalline diamond (UNCD) by hot‑filament chemical vapor deposition (proprietary method).

steps.title: 3D print recording components
steps.instruction: 3D‑print the shuttle jig, circuit‑board jacket, and motor adaptor (Formlabs Form 2, Clear Resin, catalog RS‑F2‑GPCL‑04).

steps.title: Tap threads in motor adaptor and jig
steps.instruction: Tap a 1/4"‑20 thread into the top hole of the motor adaptor (opposite the D‑hole), a 6‑32 thread into the side hole of the motor adaptor, and a 4‑40 thread into all side holes of the shuttle jig.

substeps.instruction: Tap 1/4"‑20 in motor adaptor top hole.
Tap 6‑32 in motor adaptor side hole.
Tap 4‑40 in each shuttle‑jig side hole.

steps.title: Glue threaded rod and set screws
steps.instruction: Glue a 1" 1/4"‑20 threaded rod into the top of the motor adaptor (opposite the D‑hole) and partially screw (do not glue) 1/4" 4‑40 cup‑point set screws into the shuttle‑jig side holes.

substeps.instruction: Apply UV‑curable glue to secure the 1" 1/4"‑20 rod.

steps.title: Glue nuts into circuit board holder
steps.instruction: Glue 2‑56 nuts into the hexagonal cutouts of the circuit‑board holder; optionally insert 2‑56 Torx screws on the opposite side to align the nuts while the glue cures, providing holding force for the board.

substeps.instruction: Apply UV glue to each 2‑56 nut cavity.
Insert 2‑56 Torx screws opposite side to align nuts during curing.

steps.title: Attach UNCD shuttle to jig with UV glue
steps.instruction: Using a microscope, align the UNCD shuttle with the jig guides and bond it to the jig tip with UV‑curable glue, avoiding any glue on the shuttle except the rectangular mounting section. Skip this step only if only acute recordings are needed.

steps.title: Create medial incision over lumbar spine
steps.instruction: With the animal prone, make a medial scalpel incision over the lower lumbar and sacral spine.

steps.title: Prepare 40% PEG8000 solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 3 g of 8000 MW polyethylene glycol (PEG) in 4.5 g (≈4.5 ml) DI water to make a 40 % (mass) solution; heat in a glass dish on a hot plate at 90 °C until fully dissolved, maintaining a ~1 cm depth for dip‑coating.

steps.title: Dip UNCD shuttle in 40% PEG
steps.instruction: Remove the 40 % PEG8000 mixture from heat and dip the UNCD shuttle once; allow to air‑dry for a few seconds (final PEG thickness ≈2 µm). Avoid coating the shuttle‑jig tip.

steps.title: Align array to UNCD tip with PEG4000
steps.instruction: Under a microscope, roughly align the array ribbon to the UNCD shuttle backing (≈10 µm precision) and apply a drop of 60 % PEG4000 (see next step) to secure the ribbon to the rectangular backing without wetting the tip.

steps.title: Prepare 60% PEG4000 solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 60 % (mass) PEG4000 (4 000 MW) in DI water; heat at 90 °C on a hot plate until fully dissolved.

steps.title: Dip shuttle+array in 40% PEG
steps.instruction: Remove the 40 % PEG8000 mixture from heat and dip the assembled shuttle + array into it; verify that the array remains correctly aligned.

steps.title: Add relief to array ribbon
steps.instruction: Loosen the shuttle‑jig side screws, slide the circuit‑board holder forward to create relief for the array ribbon, then retighten the screws.

steps.title: Insert circuit board and position array
steps.instruction: Place the circuit board with the mounted array into the circuit‑board holder, slide the holder’s slider into the shuttle‑jig track, and secure it with the side threaded rods so the array hangs over the jig tip onto the UNCD shuttle. Use predefined marks (15.5 mm for 20 mm array, 31.5 mm for 40 mm array) to set forward position; back out side screws if needed for free movement.

steps.title: Perform laminectomy to expose DRG
steps.instruction: After the medial incision, use rongeurs to perform a laminectomy exposing the lumbosacral spinal cord and dorsal root ganglia (typically L7‑S2); keep nerves moist throughout the procedure.

steps.title: Expose iliac crest and place bone screws
steps.instruction: Scalpel‑expose the bilateral posterior superior iliac crests, drill a hole in each bone with a Dremel, and insert self‑tapping bone screws (size chosen to match the holes).

steps.title: Set up optical stabilization board and microscope
steps.instruction: Place an optical stabilization board beneath the stand, secure it with C‑clamps, and assemble a support structure for a micromanipulator over the surgical site; mount a USB microscope (Teslong MS100) to view the DRG surface.

steps.title: Mount linear actuator to micromanipulator
steps.instruction: Attach a high‑resolution linear actuator (Physik Instrumente M‑235.DD) to the micromanipulator for precise array positioning and connect the actuator to a computer.

steps.title: Insert urethral catheter for bladder drainage
steps.instruction: Insert a urethral catheter and allow the bladder to drain into a collection receptacle.

steps.title: Secure motor adaptor to linear actuator
steps.instruction: Use a thread adaptor (Thorlabs AS4M25E, internal M4 × 0.7, external 1/4"‑20) to attach the motor adaptor to the linear actuator.

steps.title: Suspend pelvis with wire and adjust supports
steps.instruction: Wrap stainless‑steel wire around the pelvic bone screws, suspend the cat’s pelvis, lower the leg supports so the legs are extended, and ensure the spine is parallel to the table for proper lung inflation; monitor vitals and adjust as needed.

steps.title: Align shuttle tip over target DRG
steps.instruction: Use the micromanipulator to bring the shuttle tip directly over the desired dorsal root ganglion.

steps.title: Advance shuttle into DRG during breath hold
steps.instruction: Briefly suspend breathing (≤1 min), then advance the shuttle into the DRG at 1–2 mm s⁻¹ using the linear‑actuator software; immediately resume breathing and record neural activity. Expect firing to increase gradually over 1–2 h after the insertion shock. (Further steps for shuttle removal are optional.)

steps.title: Connect headstages and start recording software
steps.instruction: Connect two Ripple nano (or nano2) headstages to the circuit board, link the headstages to the Neural Interface Processor (NIP), launch the Trellis 11.1 software on Windows 10, and verify that both 32‑channel headstages are operational.

steps.title: Rinse array backing with saline
steps.instruction: Rinse the array backing with saline while watching for dissolution of the hardened PEG.

steps.title: Release array ribbon after PEG dissolution
steps.instruction: Once the PEG has dissolved, gently free the array ribbon from the shuttle jig and shuttle using fine force‑picks or a broom bristle; avoid jostling any part of the setup to prevent breakage.
